target_customer: Companies running hybrid offices that need desk reservation, attendance visibility and space right sizing
problem: As teams split time between office and home, companies did not know who would be in, could not coordinate in-person days, and kept unused office space.

founders.name: Aakhil Fardeen
previous_startups: Lish (food service for offices, co-founded 2014, CEO until December 2020)
founders.background_notes: Product leadership roles per YC and profile listings. Later joined Envoy.

founders.name: Theresa Klaassen
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page, background not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Desk booking, calendars and integrations are standard SaaS engineering. Value came from workflow and enterprise integrations, not hard technology.

defensibility.rationale: Many desk booking tools existed or launched quickly, and features were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Envoy, a larger San Francisco competitor, acquired Worksphere in September 2022 after also buying OfficeTogether.

market_need_then: The pandemic return to office planning in early 2021 created sudden demand for desk reservation and attendance tools, covered by GeekWire in 2021.

branding.domain_note: Used worksphere.com. Acquisition date or price of the domain not found.
branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt listing. No press about the brand itself found.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic compound name shared with unrelated companies, such as an Indian payroll product and an architecture firm, with no found brand press.

outcome_analysis: Worksphere launched in early 2021 into a burst of demand for hybrid office tools but faced many near identical desk booking competitors, and with under a million dollars of reported funding it sold to Envoy in September 2022, when Envoy was consolidating the category by also buying OfficeTogether. The price was not disclosed. This looks like a small team exit driven by competitive pressure and a tightening funding market rather than a breakout outcome.
notes: Company site worksphere.com returned HTTP 526 and GeekWire pages returned 403, so details come from search results. Pre-seed figures conflict: GeekWire 550 thousand dollars, FundedIQ 400 thousand dollars in 2021-04, Seedtable 380 thousand dollars in 2021-04, PitchBook 435 thousand dollars dated 2020-12, CB Insights total about 950 thousand dollars. None are recorded as rounds because they are single snippets or aggregators that disagree. Competitor search returned only 2026 comparison pages, nothing dated near the batch, so the list is empty; Envoy and Robin are named only in outcome text. Another Worksphere (India payroll) exists and was excluded.
